synthesis: Scout users authenticate with email+password via ClarityScoutAuthController::login(). Initial onboarding uses a one-shot signed URL (ScoutSetPasswordController) that expires in 7 days and becomes invalid once email_verified_at is set (line 71-72 of ScoutSetPasswordController). NO password reset or account recovery flow exists. If a user forgets their password (or email), they are permanently locked out unless an admin manually intervenes through force-login impersonation or re-grants access (which only works pre-verification per ScoutUsersResource line 368-369). The ticket requests self-serve recovery without needing to remember email. Preferred approach: adopt Clarity's magic-link/OTP system (OneTimePassword class + CustomLoginPage) which requires only email (no password), already proven in Filament panel auth. Alternative: admin-initiated password reset action in ScoutUsersResource that works post-verification. The blast radius is authentication — any bug could lock out all Scout drivers or expose accounts.

acceptance_criteria.text: Scout driver can recover account without remembering email using magic-link/OTP
acceptance_criteria.interpretation: Add 'Forgot Password' flow on Login.vue that sends OTP to entered email. Driver receives email, enters OTP, gains access without knowing password. Must handle 'forgot email' case — likely requires admin contact path since email is the recovery anchor.
acceptance_criteria.note: The 'without remembering email' constraint is tricky — OTP still requires knowing the email to receive the code. Likely interpretation: user remembers email OR contacts admin for help (AC3).

acceptance_criteria.text: Admin can assist with password reset
acceptance_criteria.interpretation: Add action to ScoutUsersResource table that generates a new set-password signed URL (similar to resend_onboarding line 356-412) but works AFTER email_verified_at is set. Email sent to driver. Action visible for all Scout users, not just unverified.

acceptance_criteria.text: Solution is consistent with Clarity (Filament) auth patterns
acceptance_criteria.interpretation: Reuse OneTimePassword class, SendOneTimePassword mailable, similar UI flow. Scout OTP email should match ScoutOnboardingNotification styling. Cache key pattern 'otp_scout_<email>' to avoid collision with Filament panel OTP.

acceptance_criteria.text: No permanent lockout — always an admin-assisted path
acceptance_criteria.interpretation: Admin force-login (already exists, line 346-354 ScoutUsersResource) + new password reset action ensure no Scout user is permanently locked out. Force-login provides immediate access; password reset provides long-term recovery.

questions.text: How should 'recover without remembering email' work?
questions.context: AC1 says user doesn't need to remember email, but OTP requires email to send the code. Options: (a) admin lookup by name/phone in ScoutUsersResource shows user's email hint (first 3 chars + domain), (b) contact-admin prompt in UI, (c) interpret AC as 'email OR magic-link' (typo for 'AND'?).
questions.recommendation: Interpret as 'email OR admin assist' — AC1 covers self-serve (OTP via remembered email), AC2 covers admin assist (for forgotten email). Add 'Contact your admin' UI hint on Login.vue when OTP fails.

questions.text: Should password auth remain alongside OTP, or replace it?
questions.context: Clarity Filament uses OTP-only (bypassed in non-prod). Scout currently password-only. Hybrid (both options) is safest rollout but adds UI complexity. Ticket says 'magic-link/OTP like Clarity' but doesn't explicitly deprecate passwords.
questions.recommendation: Implement hybrid: add OTP as second option ('Forgot Password? Use OTP' link). Deprecate password in future ticket if OTP adoption is high. Reduces rollout risk.

questions.text: Should the one-shot guard in ScoutSetPasswordController be removed or bypassed for admin resets?
questions.context: Line 71-72: if (hasVerifiedEmail) rejectWith('used'). Admin password reset needs to work post-verification. Options: (a) add 'admin_initiated' flag to signed URL params, bypass guard if set + signature valid, (b) separate admin-reset controller with no one-shot guard, (c) remove one-shot guard entirely (security regression for initial onboarding).
questions.recommendation: Option (a): add 'reset=1' param to signed URL for admin resets, bypass one-shot guard when present. Keeps onboarding secure while allowing admin resets. Document in ScoutSetPasswordController docblock.

Clarity OTP uses cache TTL of config('auth.password_timeout') seconds (default 900 = 15min). Scout should match. Cache key 'otp_scout_<email>' to avoid collision with Filament 'otp_<email>'.
Scout login is rate-limited at 'throttle:5,1' (routes/api.php:29). OTP request endpoint needs same or stricter limit to prevent email spam.
ScoutUsersResource line 368-369: resend_onboarding only visible if !email_verified_at. Admin password reset must be separate action, visible post-verification.
ScoutOnboardingNotification uses 7-day TTL (line 17). Admin reset should use same or shorter (security: reset is reactive, not proactive grant).
Login.vue currently has no 'Forgot Password' UI. Add link below password field, modal/inline form for OTP request.
Scout analytics (ScoutAnalyticsEvent) may need new events: OtpRequested, OtpLogin, PasswordReset. Check app/Enums/ScoutAnalyticsEvent.php for patterns.
OneTimePassword::attempt() (line 59-75) uses Auth::login() + Auth::refresh() (JWT). Scout uses Sanctum createToken(). Need Scout-specific OTP validation that mints Sanctum token, not JWT.
Test isolation: Scout auth tests likely use RequiresClickhouse trait (for kit/org setup). OTP flow tests can avoid CH by mocking or using factory-only fixtures.

qa_hint: Auth testing is blast-radius. Manually verify: (1) OTP email arrives, code works, expires correctly; (2) admin reset email arrives, link works post-verification, one-shot enforced; (3) force-login still works; (4) password login still works (if hybrid); (5) rate limiting prevents email spam; (6) org scoping preserved (can't reset cross-org user); (7) analytics events fire. Test on real Scout PWA (not just Postman) to catch Vue routing issues. Check email templates in multiple clients (Gmail, Outlook, mobile).
